sources.callee:
[
        "$ModuleAvailable = [bool](Get-Module -ListAvailable -Name Hyper-V | Select-Object -First 1)",
        "$ComputerInfo = Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue",
        "$OperatingSystem = Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue",
        "$HypervisorPresent = [bool]$ComputerInfo.HypervisorPresent",
        "$Vmms = Get-Service -Name vmms -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue",
        "$VmmsRunning = [bool]($Vmms -and $Vmms.Status -eq 'Running')",
        "$HyperVAdministratorsMember = $false",
        "$ManagementAccess = $false",
        "$SessionRefreshRequired = $false",
        "$CurrentUserSid = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent().User.Value",
        "try { $HyperVAdministratorsMember = [bool]@(Get-LocalGroupMember -SID ([Security.Principal.SecurityIdentifier]'S-1-5-32-578') -ErrorAction Stop | Where-Object { $_.SID.Value -eq $CurrentUserSid }).Count } catch { $HyperVAdministratorsMember = $false }",
        "if ($ModuleAvailable -and $VmmsRunning) { try { @(Get-VM -ErrorAction Stop) | Out-Null; $ManagementAccess = $true } catch { $ManagementAccess = $false } }",
        "$SessionRefreshRequired = $HyperVAdministratorsMember -and -not $ManagementAccess",
        "$LocalAppData = [Environment]::GetFolderPath([Environment+SpecialFolder]::LocalApplicationData)",
        "$QemuImg = if ($LocalAppData) { Join-Path $LocalAppData 'Android\\Sdk\\emulator\\qemu-img.exe' } else { $null }",
        // Same walk as Assert-NoReparsePath in acquisition, but it answers instead of throwing.
        "function Test-CccNoReparsePath([string]$Path) {",
        "  try {",

distributionBoundaries.acceptedArtifactScope: No fresh build/package/install execution. Source/package/embedded signatures and native assets must satisfy ACC-M13-source/install; current runtime policy migration statuses remain separate.
negativeRequirements: generated-output retirement may remove only named obsolete modules/bundles
scope/link validation must precede deletion of dist outputs
Windows-LX source links are not normal symlinks and need native adapter
rewritten package export target must stay within embedded destination and exist
package import wildcard and native asset payload must not depend on repository node_modules
installed CLI/MCP/broker binary entrypoints and declarations remain compatible
independentSourceTrace: package.json build: build packages -> assemble -> HyperV static -> roottsc+contract/real/test/architecture typing -> realtest bundles -> CLIversion substitution -> MCPbundle -> CodexCJSbundle -> assemble again.
buildWorkspacePackages validates both package source manifests+dependency entries before any link/output mutation,repairs only links,removes perpackage dist then native tsc each.

assembleWorkspaceRuntime removes specified obsolete root exports/bundle paths only; embeds hyper-v/device-lab package.json/dist/powershell and DeviceLab providers/appium-runtime while excluding node_modules.

All dist JS/TS import literals excluding real-tests are AST-resolved against manifest exact/wildcard exports; target must remain inside embedded package and exist; rewrite static/dynamic/require/importtype/import.meta.resolve literals. Dynamic nonliteral resolution is not covered.
MCP builder esbuild-wasm bundles server.mjs platformnode esm and createRequire banner; explicit root outfile dist/device-lab-mcp/server.mjs.
Codex resume entry bundled cjs targetnode20 into dist/codex-resume-runtime.cjs; invocation reads this actual shipped asset.

manifestSourceMaps.wildcardProof: *.js wildcard exposes matching generated dist subpaths including nested path substitutions; providers/* and appium-runtime/* map existing runtime asset paths. This is static source-to-build mapping; exports symbol reachability and fresh installed execution remain verification obligations.
manifestSourceMaps.expansionLimits: Manifest-controlled static source files listed by rg --files without build; expected tsc outputs listed separately. This is shipped-path coverage,not emitted artifact certification or all public symbol exports.

trace: proxy-builder copies scripts/localhost-proxy and native Go build CGO_ENABLED0 -> /usr/local/bin/ccc-proxy.
mcp-builder npmci--ignore-scripts then copies packages/MCP/buildlink helpers; workspacebuild -> MCPbundle -> assemble; final image copies dist/device-lab-mcp and dist/packages under /opt/ccc/dist.
Final appium-runtime npmci--omit=dev installs runtime dependencies in embedded package; thin /opt/ccc/device-lab-mcp/server.mjs imports packaged server.
Five clipboard shims and X11 bridge copied755 and CRLF-normalized; entrypoint shell copied755/normalized as ENTRYPOINT; CMD tail-f/dev/null.
containerImageAssets.certificate: Source mapping only; does not establish installed-byte parity/native build/provider execution.

knownContractDiscrepancies.detail: Record actual earlier global method-set refusal for base_image_create/clone, and record separate snapshot backend-method refusal for create/restore/delete. Current target lookup/DTO explanation does not describe the earliest refusal at baseline.

Observed guest key adoption exists only as a retained helper; no production caller imports/calls it. Current broker constant false and diagnostic retry preserve expected trust on changed bootstrap key.

Automatic cached manifest license gate at :1171 and fresh windows-server gate :1181; explicit create.image and dryrun branches return earlier. Record actual ordering rather than silently claiming all explicit/imported paths require automatic receipt.

retainedLibraryContract: Hyper-V typed low-level API/native PowerShell transactions remain independent retained library. Device Lab owns CCC Notes/incarnation identity, snapshot journals/replay, owner state and image allocation authority.
snapshotSupportDisposition: Native get/checkpoint/remove/restore/repair methods support complete owner workflows.
macOS clone/delete helpers, lifecycle tokens, restoreRecovery phases, sorted locks and owner repository support their workflows; no separate invented repair action.
QEMU qemu-img effect/path validation/atomic lab writes support action rows.
Public aliases and broker child isolation are non-counted.

categories.proposedLockOwner: No owner/device operation or lease mutation lock is acquired; authenticated broker reads bounded owner inventory snapshots. Android creation choices/host inventory are additional observations.

Broker lifecycleCommandInvoke holds the shared owner/stateKey/device operation lock. Owner-record publication takes the separate devices.mutation.lock; physical lease mutations retain their hardware-specific guards where invoked.

For non-dry-run invocation broker holds owner/stateKey/device operation lock, then Hyper-V host mutation lock for create/delete/start/stop/reboot or status with pending lifecycle/snapshot journal. Ordinary status omits host guard. Hyper-V dry-run returns before these acquisitions.

Broker withPhysicalDeviceOperation holds shared owner/stateKey/device operation lock. Attach/detach lease claim/release and rollback use hardware-specific lease mutation locks; owner-record mutation uses devices.mutation.lock.
categories.routeCorrection: broker.physical.attach/detach; raw broker.device.tool.invoke excludes both actions

categories.proposedLockOwner: No operation lock or provider child is reached: validateDeviceToolParams rejects this advertised private action before dispatch because it is absent from DEVICE_BROKER_TOOL_METHODS.
No provider child operation lock is reached: invokeBackendDeviceTool rejects this advertised action at the macOS backend method gate before deviceToolRunner.

Broker holds shared owner/stateKey/device operation lock across recording start/stop; recording generation publication uses devices.mutation.lock. Physical Android additionally refreshes the hardware lease.

No encompassing owner/device operation lock is acquired. Broker observes recording process identity; stale-generation cleanup uses separate owner devices.mutation.lock through transitionOwnerRecordingRuntime.
Broker delegates without acquiring owner/device operation lock; provider child acquires that shared lock through its public handler, and owner-record updates use separate repository mutation lock.

Neither broker nor provider handler acquires encompassing owner/device operation lock for recording status. Provider reconciliation may publish generation-checked update under owner repository mutation lock; Windows status may finalize/copy archive.

Public MCP listing composes device_exec and inherits selected executor lock: provider child owns shared owner/device operation lock for Android/macOS/Windows Sandbox; Hyper-V broker owns it for Windows/Linux VM. Raw list_files is refused by backend gate; Hyper-V raw refusal occurs after acquisition of its owner/device lock.
categories.proposedExecutor: MCP-composed broker-native Hyper-V or provider-child device_exec

categories.proposedLockOwner: Broker delegates to iOS Simulator provider child; handleIosTool acquires shared owner/ios/device operation lock for native app-container listing.

No owner/device operation lock or attachment lease claim is acquired. Broker deliberately invokes unattached provider child; Android observes/changes ADB transport, while iOS status observes host inventory and other wireless actions return unsupported diagnostics.

Broker holds shared owner/stateKey/device operation lock before supported-method gate and native Hyper-V tool execution. Window listing/focus recurse into guest exec under existing guard; this path does not acquire console queue or lifecycle host-wide mutation lock.

Broker holds shared owner/stateKey/device operation lock, then process-local owner/backend/device console queue. Linux type/scroll guest-exec recursion retains these guards; console queue is not file/host-wide lock.

Raw broker.device.tool.invoke delegates without encompassing owner/device operation lock; provider status reads session/discovery metadata. Physical raw dispatch briefly guards lease heartbeat before child invocation. Public explicit/implicit mobile_session_status uses unguarded broker.appium.status.
categories.proposedExecutor: provider-child for raw route; broker-native Appium observation for public route

categories.proposedLockOwner: Raw provider-child wait does not hold encompassing owner/device operation lock. iOS Appium waits briefly acquire that lock for session establishment then observe with generation/lease checks; Android waits and iOS Simulator wait-for-app observe native tools without that outer guard. Explicit broker-mobile path separately holds broker guard per Appium ensure/request RPC, not across whole polling loop.
categories.proposedExecutor: provider-child for raw route; per-RPC broker Appium for explicit public route

categories.proposedLockOwner: For raw broker.device.tool.invoke binding broker delegates to provider child; public provider handler acquires shared owner/stateKey/device operation lock when requiresOwnerDeviceOperation selects action and valid owned target exists. Physical dispatch/handler lease heartbeats retain hardware guards; owner updates retain separate repository mutation lock.

exposureVariants.detail: Explicit public mobile path uses Appium except mobile_set_network/clear_app_data/grant_permission/revoke_permission/set_battery. Broker owner/stateKey/device guard is acquired independently for ensure and each request RPC; physical lease refresh inside. Multi-request actions/waits release/reacquire between RPCs.
Implicit mobile path normally selects provider child; session status and clipboard select Appium-specific routes. Never replace all mobile lock owners globally with either executor.

Broker/provider operation paths align; provider reentrancy is process-local AsyncLocalStorage and does not allow broker to hold lock while launching child. Physical lease transaction takes hardware then aggregate mutation guard separately.
